info.title: CsMesh - Structural code intelligence for C# and .NET under a token budget.
info.description: Structural answer engine for C# codebases. Answers agent questions about call paths, interface implementations and change blast radius under a hard token budget.

options.name: --budget

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Compares the current index against the one before it, kept at .csmesh/graph.prev.json.
Run 'csmesh index' before your change and again after it.
'diff' answers what you edited. This answers what the shape of the codebase did. A
deleted AddScoped is one moved line in a diff and a missing binding here -- the
compiler catches neither, and unit tests that inject mocks do not either.
EXIT CODES:
4 when there is no previous index to compare against.

and the resulting graph will be missing edges; 'index' reports the count.

commands.description: Where the weight is: projects, entrypoints, hotspots

options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 700, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
The first command to run in a repository you do not know. 'ls' and 'tree' answer
"where are the files", which is the wrong axis: a folder name does not say whether
anything in it is load bearing. This answers which projects lean on which, where the
entrypoints cluster, and which handful of members everything runs through.
Deliberately one screen. A map that needs two is a directory listing.

commands.name: path
commands.description: Shortest route from one symbol to another (alias: why)

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 400, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --depth
options.description: Maximum hops to search (default: 12)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Answers "why is this class involved in this request". Mediator dispatch, container
bindings and interface calls each count as one hop, so the path crosses them like any
other edge. Exits 1 when no route exists within the depth limit.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Structural changes vs. a git revision, gated by an accepted baseline

options.name: --calls
options.description: Include call and construction edges (noisy; off by default)

options.name: --accept
options.description:
Write the current findings to .csmesh/accepted.txt as the new
baseline; accepted findings stop being reported until BASE moves
past them, at which point they are pruned automatically

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 800, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
'changes' compares against whatever csmesh index last saw, which is an accident of
timing. 'review' compares against a named git revision, cached per commit so a second
run is fast, which is what a pull request or a CI gate actually needs.
A binding that moved is reported; a method body that was edited without moving an edge
is not -- same three-dimensional comparison as 'changes' (added, removed, degraded).
Building the base graph checks the revision out into a disposable worktree under
.csmesh/; your own working tree, staged or not, is never touched.
EXIT CODES:
0   nothing unaccepted changed (or --accept just ran)
4   the base revision could not be indexed, or no current index exists: csmesh index
5   unaccepted structural change exists -- fail the build
64  not a git repository, or BASE does not resolve

arguments.name: BASE
arguments.description:
Revision to compare against (default: merge base with the remote's
default branch, falling back to HEAD when that cannot be resolved)

commands.name: silence
commands.description: Why a query came back empty (alias: why-not)

options.name: --depth
options.description: How far to walk before giving up (default: 12)

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 700, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Exit 1 from any other command means the graph had nothing. It does not say whether the
symbol was mistyped, lives in a package, was never bound because the solution was not
built, or is reached only through a container scan. Those call for four different next
actions.
With two symbols this reports where the walk stopped and what the indexer recorded at
each dead end, and checks whether the route exists in the other direction. With one it
reports why nothing enters or leaves it, including references that appear in source but
never bound.
EXIT CODES:
0 when there was no silence to explain -- the path exists, or the symbol is connected.
1 when the absence is real and explained.

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
'doctor' reports that a graph is, say, 91% resolved. This says which 9%. A missing
edge and an absent one look identical in every other command; this is the only place
they can be told apart. The sample is capped at 400 sites per index.

commands.name: usage
commands.description: Display local invocation metrics and caller attribution

options.name: --days
options.description: Filter invocations from the last N days (default: 7)

options.name: --tail
options.description: Show the last N invocations instead of the summary (default: 10)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output the raw invocation log as JSON

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
READING IT:
The hit rate covers only commands that resolve a symbol, because exit 1 means
something different elsewhere: from 'silence' it means a real absence was explained,
from 'diff' that nothing changed.
A high answered rate means the tool works and the question is whether anyone is
reaching for it. A high not-found rate means it is being reached for and failing,
which is a different problem. 'never used' is a read on the installed skill rather
than on the commands themselves.

commands.name: where
commands.description: Find the symbols a word belongs to, ranked by what reaches them

options.name: --under
options.description: Restrict to a subtree, e.g. --under src/Api

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 400, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Every other command takes a symbol. This is the one that finds it. Start here when the
task is described in words -- "the discount rules", "checkout" -- and end with a name
the other commands accept.
Symbol names, namespaces, file paths and route templates are all searched. Results are
ordered by how many entrypoints reach each symbol, not alphabetically: a request DTO
and the handler that consumes it match the same word, and only one of them has three
routes above it. Test code is ranked down, not hidden.
The last line is the command to run next, already filled in.
String literals, config values, TODOs and non-.cs files are not in the graph. Use grep
for those.
EXIT CODES:
0 matches found   1 nothing matched   2 over budget

EXIT CODES:
0 ok   1 not-found   2 over-budget   3 ambiguous   4 no-index   5 changed (review only)
64 usage-error   70 internal-error
CONFIDENCE:
A row marked [... ?0.70 short-name-match] came from a name match, not a compiler
symbol. Treat anything below 0.80 as a lead to verify, not a fact. 'csmesh doctor'
reports how many such edges the graph holds.
